chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: Joining Georgie Auld and suddenly fronting the band
summary: He joins Auld in Washington the day before Auld's mother dies and has to lead the band blind, after refusing a Southern tour with Kirk.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Back to Georgie Auld's band. You went out on the road with them?
Yeah. I joined the band in Washington, D.C., the day before his mother died.

Yeah. And he had to take off and go home. So he let me front the band, and I didn't know the band! I didn't have no slightest idea what was happening with the band. All I had to do was to get out in front and introduce the acts, and give the downbeats and so forth. But I really know... I felt kind of leery, because I didn't know what the band was like. But after one show, I kind of settled down and got myself settled into what was happening. But how about that? You join the band, and the guy says, "You're the leader!" -- and I don't even know what the band plays or how good they play or anything.

But I did sit in with him a couple of tunes up in Baltimore before they were... They came to Baltimore and played a dance, and Turk Van Lake was in the band. So Turk asked me did I like the band, and I told him, "Yeah, it sounds all right." So he says, "Well, we need a high note man, if you want to join the band." I had asked Billy Shaw,

Andy's manager, where was the band hitting; so he told me we were coming back to New York. Well, the night that we closed in Baltimore, he gave me a list of one-nighters, and New York was nowhere on it! I said, "Oh boy, here I am again, and we're going back down there." I said, "I can't make it down there," because I always did...I never did like prejudice. And down there, they were prejudiced, you know what I mean. So I said, "Well, shit, this is where I get off this time." So I told Jimmy Forrest and J.D. King, "Tell Andy I ain't gonna make this trip.

So I went out and joined Georgie's band. I went and played a couple of tunes with him, then he asked me did I want to join the band, and so I said, "Yeah, sure. Why not?" So he told me that they were going right to the Howard Theatre, which was right about forty miles from Baltimore. So I went over there and got me a pad, and went on it... So I was at the theatre the next day, and he called me, he told me, "You've got to run the show, man." I said, "What?" I couldn't figure that out. I said, "Well, wait, what's the matter?" He said, "Man, I lost my mother. I've got to go to New York." So I said, "Well, in that case, I guess I've got to."
But I mean, Georgie was very nice. He brought me a nice cigarette lighter when he came back!
